obernants.approximation_semantics: Source-derived exact target relation; finite evidence is not a general proof.
obernants.assumptions: Successful allocation; exact bytes and stated transformation premises.
obernants.domain: Finite byte slices and ordinary terminating Rust calls with successful allocation.
obernants.operator: In the universe of text/result pairs, exclude altered byte multiplicities, wrong sorted-rotation last columns, and noncanonical primary rows. Inverse rejects out-of-range p before any reachability check, and rejects unreachable in-range (C,p) pairs. Source-derived excluded behavior is not a semantic proof.

obernants.operator: The full canonical pair (C,p) has exactly one input text when reachable, recovered by inverse; otherwise the fiber is empty. Projection to C alone retains ambiguity: abab and baba both produce bbaa, with primary rows 0 and 2. Neither column-only reconstruction nor accepting every LF cycle recovers the original.

obernants.operator: Equal rotations of a periodic text are ordered by original offset. If the least cyclic period is d (so d divides n), each equal-rotation class has n/d members; source offset zero is first in its class. For bbaa only primary 0 or 2 is canonical; 1 and 3 are rejected despite decoding periodic candidates.

obernants.operator: LF(i)=number of column bytes less than C[i] plus count of equal bytes strictly before i. Stable occurrence numbering gives a permutation; equal symbols alone do not identify which occurrence was meant. Following LF n times from p reconstructs a candidate, not reachability certification.

obernants.operator: At width w<n, sorting (rank[i],rank[(i+w) mod n]) refines cyclic prefixes to length 2w. Once width reaches n, order of those prefixes agrees with full rotations, including equality. Saturating doubling cannot stall before reaching valid slice length n.

obernants.operator: For a strictly increasing map f of byte support, transform(f(T))=(f(C),p). Sorting equivalence and stable tie offsets survive; mere injectivity without byte-order preservation does not preserve row order.

obernants.operator: For n=0, p=0 is the sole valid metadata and decodes empty. For n>0, p>=n gives InvalidPrimaryIndex. For remaining metadata, canonical retransformation equality chooses Ok(candidate) versus InvalidTransform. These precedence partitions cover every byte column and usize primary.
